entries.expected: The case table of design Section 8.5 run against both halves: the pre-enforcement half is expected to fail, so the test discriminates, and the enforced half fills no earlier than the declared eligibility
entries.observed: The pre-enforcement half fails as expected: with no deferral the fill carries the decision bar's own timestamp and that bar's own close, and the account is debited at that instant. The enforced half holds for the latency model, whose fill is never earlier than the arrival and lands on the first bar at or after it. Two cases disagree with the table and are named here. The bridge mechanism resolves an artifact's eligibility to the next session's open and stamps the signal with it, but its submission path holds no clock, so the order set is submitted at delivery and the fill precedes the declared eligibility by the whole interval to the next session. And a deferred intent with no subsequent market data is filled at shutdown against the last known close, without notifying the strategy, where the table requires that no fill be fabricated. With bar-only data the deferral prices at a bar close rather than at an opening price, so the declared eligibility can be honoured in time but not in price unless the snapshot carries market data at that instant

Ranking: every one of the 45 decisions whose cross-section holds all four instruments selects (AAPL.NASDAQ, MSFT.NASDAQ) in that order, no other name is ever selected or signalled, the orders are 2500 AAPL and 2631 MSFT filled at 100.00 and 95.00, and the only open positions at the end are AAPL and MSFT. Holding period: with the entry at period S = 3 there is no exit at S + 1, there is a flatten at S + 2, and the exit periods are S + 2, S + 4, S + 6 and S + 8, so the cap is counted in decision periods, is reset by the new entry, and never fires part-way through a period. Rebalance schedule: 48 decisions over 12 periods carry the rebalance flag exactly twice, on the first decision of 2022-01-03 and of 2022-01-10, and no LONG signal is submitted on any other decision. Target allocation: the weights are 0.25, 0.25 and 0.16666666666666666 against the pre-cap shares 3/6, 2/6 and 1/6, summing to 0.6666666666666666 within the ceiling, and the strengths are 1.0, 1.0 and 0.6666666666666666, each equal to min(weight / cap, 1.0). No eligible instruments: each of the 48 decisions has an empty selection, no signal, no order, no fill and no position, so the correct behaviour is that nothing happened rather than that the run completed. Opening gap: the entry is read from the platform's own closed position at an average entry price of 100.00, the stop threshold is 90.00, the only exit decision is the first close at or below it, and the fill that follows is 70.00, strictly 20.00 below the threshold, which is the signature of the platform's own fill rather than a fill fabricated at the threshold. The stated tolerances are absolute 1e-12 for a weight or a strength, which carry one decimal-to-float conversion at the Target boundary, absolute 1e-9 for a fill price, which is two-decimal text, and exact for selections, instrument sets, exit tuples, rebalance flags, counts and position quantities, for which a tolerance would hide a difference rather than bound it. One finding is carried rather than a disagreement: the reference strategies' declared full-unit ceiling is not expressible, because portfolio.max_position_weight is bounded to 0.005 through 0.25 by the first-release policy and a payload declaring 1.0 is refused with value_out_of_bound, so the fixture declares the admitted ceiling and hand-computes every weight after the position cap has clamped it, stating both the pre-cap share and the emitted weight

entries.test_or_fixture: python/tests/integration/test_discovery_feature_parity.py, eight tests: the value, both timestamps, units and identity against the research path; the warm-up divergence; the availability lag; membership at the decision instant; the offline panel against the stream; a series shorter than the lookback; the declared skip; and the refused operator
entries.procedure: cd python && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python/.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest tests/integration/test_discovery_feature_parity.py -q (8 passed in 1.18 s), over twelve in-process daily AAPL.XNAS bars at a venue with a zero maker and taker fee, no catalog snapshot and no seed
entries.expected: One fixture computes a feature offline through the research path and evaluates it at decision time through the interpreter, and the two agree on value, observation and availability timestamps, warm-up behaviour, missing-value treatment, units and universe membership
entries.observed: The decision-time values agree with the research path on every reading the series produces: the same values, the same observation and availability timestamps, the same price unit label and the same definition digest. Four behaviours beyond agreement are measured rather than assumed. The repository's own indicator reports 0.0 for the four bars before the lookback is satisfied, and the decision-time contract serves nothing there, so a warm-up reading can never be acted on as a value. A definition with a one-day availability lag is served one bar after the bar it describes and carries its own observation instant, so a publication lag is not a look-ahead. Membership is read at the decision instant: an instrument that leaves the universe keeps receiving values while every snapshot after the exit reports it as a non-member. A series shorter than the lookback yields no value and no panel row, so an absent value is absent rather than zero, and the offline panel carries exactly one row per served reading, stamped at the observation it holds, with no row for a warm-up bar

entries.test_or_fixture: python/tests/unit/discovery/test_strategy.py, thirty-two tests: twenty-one for the allocation's declared rules, one for determinism and immutability, nine for the selection contract, and one for the rebalance schedule's period key

entries.expected: The same selection, weights, positions and versioned policy produce the same targets, with deterministic tie-breaks; each of the nine allocation decisions of Section 9.7 is exercised, including ranking ties, a missing feature, a halted security, position and sector caps binding against each other, a partial fill, a cash constraint, eligible instruments fewer than the requested portfolio size, and a held position leaving the selected set
entries.observed: Every declared rule has a case that fails if the rule is reversed, and the cases are written against the numbers rather than against the implementation: the declared tie rule orders by the feature's value descending and resolves equal values by instrument identifier ascending, a second rule orders by identifier alone, and a rank bound larger than the eligible set takes the eligible set; the position cap clamps without redistributing while the sector cap scales a sector proportionally and an undeclared sector is the instrument itself, and the two caps bind in the declared order; the gross cap scales the already-clamped weights; leave_idle leaves the capped residual uninvested and reallocate redistributes it without exceeding a cap, including the case where no instrument has headroom and the loop must stop; a selection shorter than the portfolio size is not padded and a longer one keeps the ranked leaders; a repeated identifier is weighted once at its first position; a partial fill does not change the next allocation; and an ineligible holding is flattened when the rule says so and left with no target when it does not. An instrument whose feature value was missing produces no row, so it can never be selected - the row contract this fixture pins, which FX-M3-4 then observes for an absent value and FX-M3-1 for a warm-up period. Determinism is asserted by calling the allocation three times over one request that exercises the caps and the reallocating cash policy: the field tuples are identical, the target objects are distinct instances, the request's own held-weight and sector mappings are unchanged afterwards, the emitted targets come back ordered by instrument identifier, each carries its weight and the decision's timestamps, and the same request always produces the same tuple
